subject: CareFlow v2: runtime & schema onboarding / kickoff
messages:
From: Claire Reynolds <claire@healthlytics.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dan Wu <dan.wu@healthlytics.io>, Rajesh Gupta <r.gupta@consult4health.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff request — CareFlow v2 runtime & structured outputs

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for making time. We’re ready to start the formal handoff for CareFlow v2. Key asks from our side: streaming ingest with sub-200ms tail latency for short interactions, function/tool calling to create tickets and lookup patient records, and a stabilized JSON schema for structured outputs (billing codes + diagnoses mapping).

Attached are two files to help the kickoff: CareFlow_event_schema_v1.json (schema draft) and careflow_sample_payloads.ndjson (1k sample events). We’d like a 60-minute technical kickoff next week that covers: runtime expectations, schema alignment, function naming and auth model, and an action plan for acceptance tests.

Availability: Sep 10 (morning PT) or Sep 12 (afternoon PT).

Could you propose an agenda and call attendees from your side (dev + CS + implementation)? Also let us know anything else we should prep.

—Claire
Claire Reynolds
Product Manager, Healthlytics
claire@healthlytics.io
+1 415-555-0142

Hi Claire —

Thanks — got the schema and samples. Happy to run the kickoff next week. Proposed 60-minute agenda (can tighten):
1) 5 min introductions & success criteria (Hannah/Claire)
2) 15 min runtime expectations & SLOs (Marcus) — latency targets, batching, KV cache behavior
3) 20 min structured output schema walkthrough (Kimberly) — fields, enums, validation, versioning strategy
4) 10 min function/tool calling patterns (Jasmine) — name conventions, auth, error semantics
5) 10 min acceptance tests & next steps (all)

Attendees from our side: Hannah (CS lead), Jasmine (implementation engineer), Kimberly (schema lead), Marcus (runtime eng). Please confirm which slot you prefer and whether we should invite your eng lead.

If you can drop a short list of acceptance test scenarios (e.g., hospital admits, billing reconciliation, patient lookup failure), we’ll draft the test harness.

I’ll attach an initial meeting doc (link below) and draft an action tracker during the call.

Thanks,
Hannah

From: Claire Reynolds <claire@healthlytics.io>

Cc: Dan Wu <dan.wu@healthlytics.io>, Rajesh Gupta <r.gupta@consult4health.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff request — CareFlow v2 runtime & structured outputs

Hannah —

Sep 12 afternoon PT works best. Please book 60 minutes starting 1:00pm PT. I’ve invited our engineering lead (Dan) and our consulting partner (Rajesh) so we can cover edge cases.

Acceptance scenarios from our side (brief):
- Admit event: event contains patient_id, admit_time, and initial_diagnosis (should map to ICD-10)
- Billing code enrichment: generate billing_code suggestions in the structured output array; we’ll validate against our oracle
- Create ticket flow: when an enrichment fails, call a function to create a care ops ticket with payload {patient_id, issue_code, source_event_id}
- Streaming backpressure: ensure bursts (500 events/s for 20s) do not exceed 2s tail p95 (if batching occurs we understand some increase)

I uploaded a short snippet of the event we produce for admits in the Drive folder (careflow_sample_payloads.ndjson). Rajesh included some mapping notes in his reply.

—Claire

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Reynolds <claire@healthlytics.io>, Dan Wu <dan.wu@healthlytics.io>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff request — CareFlow v2 runtime & structured outputs

Claire / Dan —

Thanks for the examples. A few technical notes ahead of the kickoff so we have shared context:
- Runtime config: we will recommend a "low-latency" profile for short interactions (target p95 <200ms) with a 20ms scheduling quantum; for burst windows we’ll enable adaptive batching up to 64 tokens/request and prefer prefix KV caching for repeated patient context. Marcus will confirm GPU selection during the call.
- Function/tool calling: propose these function names and payload shapes:
  - redwood.create_ticket(payload): payload = {"patient_id": "string", "issue_code": "string", "source_event_id": "string", "metadata": {"received_at": "iso8601"}}
  - redwood.lookup_patient(identifier): payload = {"identifier_type": "mrn|ssn|email", "identifier": "string"}

  Error handling: functions should return 2xx with a status field or 4xx/5xx for hard failures. We will wire idempotency via source_event_id.
- Schema: Kimberly, we noticed event.sample.admit.initial_diagnosis is free-text in your draft. For deterministic mapping we’d like an enum-ish field diagnosis_code (ICD10) and a fallback text field. We can add a nullable diagnosis_code field to the event schema.

Quick example of a structured output we’d emit (inline):

{"event_id":"evt_20260910_0001","patient_id":"p_9834","structured_output":[{"entry_type":"billing_suggestion","billing_code":"Z99.89","confidence":0.82}],"created_at":"2026-09-10T09:00:00Z"}

I’ll bring a runbook for the acceptance tests and a short checklist for the function auth model (API key vs mTLS).

—Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Kickoff request — CareFlow v2 runtime & structured outputs

Claire —

Booked for Sep 12, 1:00pm PT (calendar invite sent). Below is a short pre-kickoff checklist / action items to keep the meeting effective:

Owner: Healthlytics (pre-meeting)
- Confirm which admit event variants we should prioritize (ED admit vs scheduled admit) — Claire
- Flag any PII handling constraints (PII fields and retention windows) — Dan

Owner: Redwood (pre-meeting)
- Draft acceptance test harness and share runbook link — Jasmine (done, will share during call)
- Propose final schema edits (diagnosis_code enum + fallback text) — Kimberly
- Verify runtime node type & expected p95 under sample load — Marcus

Meeting goal: align on schema contract, agree function names & error model, and finalize acceptance criteria + timeline for a 2-week pilot. If we get alignment in the kickoff we’ll follow with: 1) a small pilot using 5k sample events, 2) two acceptance test runs, 3) go/no-go decision.

I’ll attach the meeting doc to the invite (Drive link above) and add an action tracker to the doc. If you want us to include a short pre-recorded demo of the function-call flow, say the word and we’ll record 10 mins.

See you Sep 12 — thanks all.

Regards,
Hannah
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Hannah Schmitt
